entities.name: Aloys von Kaunitz-Rietberg
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aloys Wenzel Dominik, Prince of Kaunitz-Rietberg (1798-1848) was a German nobleman and a diplomat of the Austrian Empire. He served as Ambassador to France from 1825 to 1828 and played a key role in the Congress of Vienna (1815), where he contributed to the reorganization of Europe after the Napoleonic Wars. Kaunitz-Rietberg's diplomatic efforts helped establish the principle of collective security, which became a cornerstone of European diplomacy in the 19th century.

As a member of the imperial family, Kaunitz-Rietberg was deeply invested in the preservation of the Habsburg Empire's power and influence. He was a strong advocate for the Austrian Empire's interests in the Congress of Vienna, where he worked closely with other European leaders to shape the post-Napoleonic order.

Despite his significant contributions to European diplomacy, Kaunitz-Rietberg's life was marked by personal tragedy. He died on November 15, 1848, at the age of 50, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most influential diplomats of his era.

In the aftermath of his death, Kaunitz-Rietberg's diplomatic efforts were hailed as a model for future generations of diplomats. His commitment to collective security and his role in shaping the Congress of Vienna have made him an important figure in the study of European diplomacy and international relations.
